text: Personalizing a text-to-image model must retain a particular subject without reducing generation to its few reference views. DreamBooth fine-tunes pretrained diffusion models on three to five images, pairing a rare-token identifier with a class descriptor so the learned instance can draw on the model's class knowledge. To prevent that class from collapsing into the instance, a prior-preservation loss rehearses class images generated by the frozen model. We implement this approach with Imagen and Stable Diffusion and release a 30-subject dataset and evaluation protocol, proposing DINO similarity to measure subject distinctions that text-aligned image embeddings may overlook. Across 3,000 generated images, Stable Diffusion DreamBooth increases DINO similarity from 0.569 to 0.668 and CLIP prompt alignment from 0.255 to 0.305 over Textual Inversion, supporting subject retention together with prompt responsiveness. Users likewise prefer DreamBooth for subject fidelity (68% versus 22%) and prompt fidelity (81% versus 12%). An Imagen ablation shows that prior preservation reduces class collapse and increases diversity while slightly lowering subject fidelity. Examples include new contexts, viewpoints, artistic renditions, and property changes; rare contexts, appearance entanglement, overfitting, and hallucinated details limit these capabilities.

Toolformer learns when and how to call text-based tools by treating their usefulness for predicting subsequent text as supervision. From a few demonstrations per API, a language model samples and executes calls, retaining responses only when they reduce prediction loss relative to both no call and a call without its result. Fine-tuning on the augmented texts teaches tool use without downstream-task demonstrations. We fine-tune GPT-J with question answering, Wikipedia search, calculator, translation, and calendar APIs. Prompted zero-shot tests permit at most one call and trigger calls when their start token ranks among the ten most likely. On ASDiv, first-number accuracy is 40.4% with tools versus 14.8% with calls disabled and 14.0% for GPT-3 (175B); the enabled-disabled contrast shows that access to tools adds benefit beyond tool-annotated training. Factual completion, question answering, and temporal tasks improve over GPT-J baselines, including on the new template-generated DATESET. Question answering still trails GPT-3, while translation aids Toolformer without consistently surpassing original GPT-J. With calls disabled, language-modeling perplexity matches content-matched fine-tuning without API annotations. Three-tool scaling experiments place most tool benefits around 775M parameters, with search an exception. Chained and interactive tool use remain unsupported.

Toolformer learns tool-use decisions from a language model's prediction loss rather than task-specific supervision. Given a few demonstrations per tool, the model proposes calls and retains them when executed responses improve subsequent token prediction over both no-call and call-only alternatives. Fine-tuning on this augmented text turns the model's own feedback into supervision for tool selection, arguments, and response incorporation. With GPT-J and five text-based APIs, prompted zero-shot evaluation encourages calls during decoding but allows at most one per input. ASDiv accuracy is 40.4%, versus 9.6% after text-only fine-tuning and 14.8% with Toolformer's calls disabled, showing that augmented fine-tuning alone does not account for the tool-enabled gain. Factual completion and temporal results improve; question answering exceeds GPT-J baselines but remains below GPT-3, and translation helps without consistently surpassing unmodified GPT-J. With calls disabled, perplexity matches text-only fine-tuning on both evaluated corpora. A GPT-2 sweep places useful tool use near 775M parameters, except for search; stronger base models can diminish weaker tools' utility. Independent call generation leaves chained and interactive tool use unsupported.

DreamBooth personalizes a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model from three to five images, preserving a subject's identity across new contexts and poses. Fine-tuning associates a rare-token identifier with the subject and its class, drawing on the class prior to generate variations beyond the observed views. A prior-preservation loss uses class-only prompts and images generated by the original model to counteract collapse of the class into the personalized instance. We release an evaluation suite of 30 subjects and 25 prompts per subject, with a DINO-based metric for distinguishing individuals within a class. With Stable Diffusion for both methods, DreamBooth exceeds Textual Inversion in DINO similarity (0.668 versus 0.569) and text-image CLIP similarity (0.305 versus 0.255). Together with majority-vote human preferences of 68% for subject fidelity and 81% for prompt fidelity, these comparisons support retaining identity while responding to new descriptions. Imagen ablations show that prior preservation reduces class collapse and increases diversity, but slightly lowers subject fidelity. Qualitative examples show artistic renditions, novel views, and property changes; context-appearance entanglement, overfitting, and hallucinated details limit identity preservation.
